items.title: Natural Lighting
items.description: Using sunlight, skylight, and available ambient daylight as primary illumination.
definitions: Create authentic, cost-efficient looks while managing time-of-day and weather constraints.
rules: Do not use when: When schedule cannot follow sun
Do not use when: When color/contrast must be studio-locked
decisionRules: Avoid when: When schedule cannot follow sun
Avoid when: When color/contrast must be studio-locked
examples: Golden-hour product lifestyle with reflector fill

items.title: Artificial Lighting
items.description: Controlled electric sources—LED, tungsten, HMI, practicals—shaped for production.
definitions: Deliver repeatable, schedule-independent illumination with precise creative control.
rules: Do not use when: When natural light alone meets look and schedule
decisionRules: Avoid when: When natural light alone meets look and schedule
commonMistakes: Ignoring fixture flicker at camera shutter
troubleshooting: Limitation: Can look unnatural if overlit
examples: LED softbox key + negative fill for clean ecommerce

items.title: Three-Point Lighting
items.description: Classic key, fill, and back/rim arrangement that models subjects with controlled depth.
definitions: Build a reliable portrait/product baseline that separates subject from background.
rules: Use when: Product heroes needing form
Do not use when: When a single motivated practical is the style
Do not use when: Documentary available-light only
bestPractices: Back light for separation not hotspot hair
workflow: Back light for separation not hotspot hair
decisionRules: Use when: Product heroes needing form
Avoid when: When a single motivated practical is the style
troubleshooting: Limitation: Can look formulaic if unchanged
Limitation: Needs space for three positions
recommendations: Back light for separation not hotspot hair
examples: Interview: soft key 45°, weak fill, subtle hair light

items.title: Key Light
items.description: The primary illumination that defines form, exposure anchor, and dominant direction.
definitions: Establish the main modeling light that viewers read as the scene’s light logic.
rules: Use when: When one direction must own the look
Do not use when: When intentionally silhouette-only with no key
decisionRules: Use when: When one direction must own the look
Avoid when: When intentionally silhouette-only with no key
troubleshooting: Limitation: Wrong angle creates unflattering shadows
examples: 45° elevated soft key for beauty; hard side key for drama

items.title: Fill Light
items.description: Secondary light or bounce that lifts shadows without overpowering the key.
definitions: Control contrast and retain detail in shadow side while preserving key direction.
rules: Use when: Product label detail in shadows
Do not use when: Low-key drama needing deep shadows
Do not use when: When neg fill is the creative choice
bestPractices: Start with bounce/neg before adding a second lamp
Keep fill softer and dimmer than key
workflow: Start with bounce/neg before adding a second lamp
Keep fill softer and dimmer than key
decisionRules: Use when: Product label detail in shadows
Avoid when: Low-key drama needing deep shadows
Avoid when: When neg fill is the creative choice
commonMistakes: Fill from wrong side creating second nose shadow
recommendations: Start with bounce/neg before adding a second lamp
Keep fill softer and dimmer than key
examples: White card fill opposite soft key for ecommerce

items.title: Back Light
items.description: Light from behind the subject toward camera, used for separation and edge definition.
definitions: Detach subject from background and add dimensional polish.
rules: Use when: Dark wardrobes on dark sets
Do not use when: When flare/halo ruins product clarity
Do not use when: Lens-facing spill uncontrolled
decisionRules: Use when: Dark wardrobes on dark sets
Avoid when: When flare/halo ruins product clarity
examples: Gentle backlight separating navy blazer from charcoal wall

items.title: Rim Light
items.description: A focused edge highlight outlining the subject’s contour.
definitions: Create a crisp silhouette edge for premium, graphic, or dramatic emphasis.
rules: Do not use when: Soft documentary naturalism
Do not use when: When reflections already outline chrome products
decisionRules: Avoid when: When reflections already outline chrome products
examples: Cool rim on black sneaker edges against void background

items.title: Soft Lighting
items.description: Large relative source size producing gradual shadow transitions and gentle modeling.
definitions: Flatter skin, reduce texture harshness, and create approachable commercial beauty.
rules: Do not use when: Gritty texture emphasis
Do not use when: Hard architectural drama
bestPractices: Increase source size relative to subject
Use diffusion close for softer look
workflow: Increase source size relative to subject
Use diffusion close for softer look
commonMistakes: Soft light too frontal and flat
troubleshooting: Limitation: Can flatten without contrast control
recommendations: Increase source size relative to subject
Use diffusion close for softer look
examples: Large octabox key for skincare campaign

items.title: Hard Lighting
items.description: Small relative source creating sharp shadows and strong specular contrast.
definitions: Reveal texture, carve dramatic shape, and signal intensity or grit.
rules: Do not use when: Unflattering beauty without makeup/control
Do not use when: When labels must stay evenly readable
decisionRules: Avoid when: Unflattering beauty without makeup/control
Avoid when: When labels must stay evenly readable
examples: Hard side light raking across leather grain

items.title: High-Key Lighting
items.description: Bright, low-contrast lighting with lifted shadows and often light backgrounds.
definitions: Communicate openness, optimism, cleanliness, and airy brand energy.
rules: Do not use when: Mystery/thriller tones
Do not use when: When deep contrast sells luxury drama
decisionRules: Avoid when: When deep contrast sells luxury drama
examples: White cyclorama soft wrap for apparel

items.title: Low-Key Lighting
items.description: Dark-dominant lighting with selective highlights and deep shadows.
definitions: Create drama, secrecy, premium night aesthetics, and focused attention.
rules: Do not use when: Informational demos needing full readability
Do not use when: High-key brand systems
bestPractices: Light what matters; crush what doesn’t
workflow: Light what matters; crush what doesn’t
decisionRules: Avoid when: Informational demos needing full readability
recommendations: Light what matters; crush what doesn’t
examples: Single hard key on watch face in void

items.title: Color Temperature
items.description: The Kelvin character of light sources—from warm tungsten to cool daylight—and how mixes read on camera.
definitions: Design color mood and keep multi-source color coherent for grade and brand.
rules: Do not use when: Ignoring Kelvin then fighting in grade only
decisionRules: Avoid when: Ignoring Kelvin then fighting in grade only
troubleshooting: Limitation: Mixed temps need intentional motivation
examples: 3200K interior practicals with matched LED key

items.title: White Balance
items.description: Aligning camera color interpretation to lighting so neutrals and brand colors stay accurate (lighting-side practice).
definitions: Ensure lighting and camera agree on white so skin and product color remain trustworthy.
rules: Use when: Brand color critical work
Do not use when: Intentional creative WB shifts without documentation
decisionRules: Use when: Brand color critical work
Avoid when: Intentional creative WB shifts without documentation
troubleshooting: Limitation: Cannot fix badly mixed lighting alone
examples: Custom WB under 5600K soft key for true packaging white

items.title: Shadows
items.description: Designed absence of light that reveals form, depth, and mood.
definitions: Use shadow shape and density as compositional and storytelling tools—not accidents.
rules: Do not use when: When critical text falls into unreadable shadow
bestPractices: Keep story-critical detail above noise floor
workflow: Keep story-critical detail above noise floor
decisionRules: Avoid when: When critical text falls into unreadable shadow
troubleshooting: Limitation: Noise and crushed detail if uncontrolled
recommendations: Keep story-critical detail above noise floor
examples: Single shadow under bottle for grounded product beauty

items.title: Reflections
items.description: Managing specular reflections on glossy, chrome, glass, and wet surfaces.
definitions: Make reflective products readable and premium by shaping what the surface mirrors.
rules: Do not use when: Ignoring reflection as ‘fix later’ on hero chrome
bestPractices: Light the reflection, not only the object
Use large soft sources and black cards
workflow: Light the reflection, not only the object
Use large soft sources and black cards
decisionRules: Avoid when: Ignoring reflection as ‘fix later’ on hero chrome
recommendations: Light the reflection, not only the object
Use large soft sources and black cards
examples: Graduated white card reflection on smartphone face

items.title: Product Lighting
items.description: Lighting strategies that prove form, material, label readability, and desirability of products.
definitions: Sell the product’s physical truth and brand promise through controlled light.
rules: Do not use when: Lifestyle-only plates where product is incidental background
decisionRules: Avoid when: Lifestyle-only plates where product is incidental background
troubleshooting: Limitation: Can look sterile without lifestyle accents
examples: Soft overhead + side accent + controlled base reflection for cosmetics

items.title: Portrait Lighting
items.description: Lighting patterns and modifiers optimized for faces—Rembrandt, loop, butterfly, split, and wrap.
definitions: Flatter or characterize people while keeping eyes alive and skin tones believable.
rules: Do not use when: When silhouettes are the intent
Do not use when: Group scenes needing even broad light only
decisionRules: Avoid when: When silhouettes are the intent
Avoid when: Group scenes needing even broad light only
examples: Soft loop lighting for CEO interview

items.title: Indoor Lighting
items.description: Controlling interiors with practicals, windows, and supplemental fixtures.
definitions: Build believable interior ambience while maintaining exposure and color control.
rules: Do not use when: When full daylight exterior is the plate
decisionRules: Avoid when: When full daylight exterior is the plate
examples: Lamp practical as motivated key with soft augmentation

items.title: Outdoor Lighting
items.description: Shaping daylight and adding portable fixtures for exterior control.
definitions: Keep outdoor images consistent and flattering despite sun movement and weather.
rules: Use when: Event coverage with sun
Do not use when: When interiors are primary
decisionRules: Use when: Event coverage with sun
Avoid when: When interiors are primary
examples: Silk overhead + reflector fill for midday interview
